title: What every involution gives, and what it does not — 8 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
What every involution gives, and what it does not. 8 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/involution.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 28 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: all (7), fixedPoints (3), constantSum (3), nine (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/involution.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 980210d1-24d9-8a7f-a759-3e28e4faa442. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (8, 4, 5, 4, 1, 6, 3). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: priorart.lean (3 observed, 0.77 expected, lift 3.92), coin.lean (3 observed, 1.02 expected, lift 2.94), fnv.lean (3 observed, 1.02 expected, lift 2.94). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.2 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 25.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.39; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.48. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 83213ac8f1ad (2026-09-15), over 659 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. That a permutation of order two decomposes a finite set into fixed points and transpositions, and that the number of fixed points therefore matches the parity of the set, is classical and long predates this deposit. It is the orbit-counting argument in any first course. What is this deposit's own here is the EXHAUSTIVE decision over ℤ/9 and the measured refusal below. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. there_are_2620_involutions_of_nine — all.length = 2620 record
  2. the_fuel_was_not_the_limit — (matchings 11 nine).length = all.length record
  3. every_involution_fixes_at_least_one_point — all.all (fun m => fixedPoints m ≥ 1) record
  4. the_fixed_points_are_always_odd — all.all (fun m => fixedPoints m % 2 == 1) record
  5. no_single_point_is_fixed_by_all — nine.all (fun d => ¬ all.all (fun m => m.contains (d, d))) record
  6. the_constant_sum_is_rare — (all.filter constantSum).length = 90 record
  7. so_involutions_are_not_all_harmonic_in_that_sense — ¬ all.all constantSum record
  8. the_coins_reflection_is_harmonic_and_is_one_of_the_ninety — constantSum coinLike = true ∧ fixedPoints coinLike = 1 ∧ (swaps coinLike).all (fun p => p.1 + p.2 == 9) record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 83213ac8f1ad and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
